distractors: Scaffolding put up to get something built and taken away again once the thing stands on its own.
The outermost layer users actually touch, where a system's decisions turn into buttons and screens and everything underneath is hidden from view.
A shared vocabulary that lets separate teams describe the same data in the same words, so a number means one thing in every report it turns up in and the arguments about definitions stop.

A part that can be pulled out and replaced while the system around it keeps running, which is a property of how it is attached rather than of where it sits. What it buys you is the ability to change something without a window.

The smallest set of features that lets a product go in front of real users at all, chosen so that what comes back is a judgement about the idea rather than about the polish. Everything left out is a bet that nobody will miss it yet.
